summary: Writes POP contents to the native lossless .pop format or interchange formats such as OBJ, EXR, PLY, SPZ, and E57. It supports single-file writes, file sequences, recording, frame pulses, selected attributes, and primitive inclusion.

key_concepts: File Out POP writes POP contents to the native .pop format and interchange formats including OBJ, EXR, PLY, SPZ, and E57.
The native .pop format is an exact representation of POP primitive types, attributes, groups, and Dimension.
Type selects single-file writes or file-sequence recording; Record, Record Pulse, Pause, Add Frame, length limits, suffix controls, and max active saves control the write lifecycle.
Format support differs: OBJ requires P(float3) and has specific normal/texture handling, SPZ requires P, Color, Scale, and Rot, and EXR/PLY can write arbitrary point attributes.
Interchange-format support differs; when not using native .pop, planner output should verify which point, vertex, and primitive data the destination format preserves.
Attribute sequence blocks and output color-space controls let the card describe exactly which attributes become file fields.
common_gotchas: OBJ requires P(float3), and only OBJ supports vertex Normal/Texture writing in the documented way.
SPZ requires specific attributes such as P, Color, Scale, and Rot.
Primitive attributes are not written by every interchange format, so bake critical primitive data to supported point attributes when needed.
Native .pop preserves the full POP but can create large files for high-capacity or attribute-heavy data.
